arxiv-1703-03861.title: Building Automated Vandalism Detection Tools for Wikidata Conference: WWW’17 Companion, April 3–7, 2017, Perth, Australia.
arxiv-1703-03861.creator: Amir Sarabadani Aaron Halfaker Dario Taraborelli
arxiv-1703-03861.description: Abstract Wikidata, like Wikipedia, is a knowledge base that anyone can edit. This open collaboration model is powerful in that it reduces barriers to participation and allows a large number of people to contribute. However, it exposes the knowledge base to the risk of vandalism and low-quality contributions.

arxiv-2109-07006.title: BME Submission for SIGMORPHON 2021 Shared Task 0. A Three Step Training Approach with Data Augmentation for Morphological Inflection
arxiv-2109-07006.creator: Gábor SzolnokBudapest University ofTechnology and Economics szolnokgabcsi@gmail.com, Botond BartaBudapest University ofTechnology and Economics b.botond25@gmail.com, Dorina LakatosBudapest University ofTechnology and Economics dorinapetra@gmail.com Judit ÁcsBudapest University ofTechnology and Econo
arxiv-2109-07006.description: Abstract We present the BME submission for the SIGMORPHON 2021 Task 0 Part 1, Generalization Across Typologically Diverse Languages shared task. We use an LSTM encoder-decoder model with three step training that is first trained on all languages, then fine-tuned on each language families and finally fine-tuned on individual languages.

arxiv-2212-09667.title: Foveate, Attribute, and Rationalize: Towards Physically Safe and Trustworthy AI Warning: This paper contains examples of potentially offensive and harmful text.
arxiv-2212-09667.creator: Alex Mei*, Sharon Levy*, William Yang Wang
arxiv-2212-09667.description: Abstract † † *Equal contribution. Users’ physical safety is an increasing concern as the market for intelligent systems continues to grow, where unconstrained systems may recommend users dangerous actions that can lead to serious injury. Covertly unsafe text is an area of particular interest, as such text may arise from everyday scenarios and are challenging to detect as harmful.

arxiv-2307-15247.title: Is this model reliable for everyone? Testing for strong calibration
arxiv-2307-15247.creator: Jean FengAlexej GossmannRomain Pirracchio, Nicholas Petrick, Gene Pennello, Berkman Sahiner
arxiv-2307-15247.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Jean FengAlexej GossmannRomain Pirracchio, Nicholas Petrick, Gene Pennello, Berkman Sahiner. In a well-calibrated risk prediction model, the average predicted probability is close to the true event rate for any given subgroup. Such models are reliable across heterogeneous populations and satisfy strong notions of algorithmic fairness. However, the task of auditing a model for strong calibration is well-known to be difficult—particularly for machine learning (ML) algorithms—due to the sheer number of potential subgroups.

arxiv-2311-00730.title: What is the physical origin of the gradient flow structure of variational fracture models?
arxiv-2311-00730.description: Abstract We investigate a physical characterization of the gradient flow structure of variational fracture models for brittle materials: a Griffith-type fracture model and an irreversible fracture phase field model. We derive the Griffith-type fracture model by assuming that the fracture energy in Griffith’s theory is an increasing function of the crack tip velocity.

arxiv-2408-10086.title: ARMADA: Attribute-Based Multimodal Data Augmentation
arxiv-2408-10086.creator: Xiaomeng Jin Jeonghwan Kim † Yu Zhou Kuan-Hao Huang Te-Lin Wu ‡ Nanyun Peng ‡ Heng Ji †, † University of Illinois, Urbana Champaign University of California, Los Angeles
arxiv-2408-10086.description: Abstract In Multimodal Language Models (MLMs), the cost of manually annotating high-quality image-text pair data for fine-tuning and alignment is extremely high. While existing multimodal data augmentation frameworks propose ways to augment image-text pairs, they either suffer from semantic inconsistency between texts and images, or generate unrealistic images, causing knowledge gap with real world examples.

arxiv-2410-02662.title: Axion-photon conversion down to the nonrelativistic regime
arxiv-2410-02662.creator: Clemente Smarra, Pierluca Carenza
arxiv-2410-02662.description: Abstract In the presence of a magnetic field, axions can convert into photons and vice versa. The phenomenology of the conversion is captured by a system of two coupled Klein-Gordon equations, which, assuming that the axion is relativistic, is usually recast into a pair of first-order Schrödinger-like equations.

arxiv-2412-07605.title: Fast Track to Winning Tickets: Repowering One-Shot Pruning for Graph Neural Networks
arxiv-2412-07605.creator: Yanwei Yue, Guibin Zhang, Haoran Yang, Dawei Cheng ‡
arxiv-2412-07605.description: Abstract Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) demonstrate superior performance in various graph learning tasks, yet their wider real-world application is hindered by the computational overhead when applied to large-scale graphs. To address the issue, the Graph Lottery Hypothesis (GLT) has been proposed, advocating the identification of subgraphs and subnetworks, i.e. , winning tickets, without compromising performance.

pmc-12641246.title: A continuous flow process for the Ireland–Claisen rearrangement
pmc-12641246.creator: Joseph D'Attoma, Stéphane Bostyn, Sylvain Routier, Karen Plé, Frédéric Buron
pmc-12641246.description: Herein, we describe an in-depth study of an enantioselective Ireland–Claisen rearrangement using a continuous flow reactor. The use of this innovative technology led to a rapid reaction at room temperature, enabling the stereocontrolled synthesis of vicinal stereogenic centers with little to no loss in yield or optical purity, in the absence of cryogenic conditions.

pmc-12731431.title: Vestibulocochlear Neuritis as a Paradoxical Reaction in an Immunocompetent Patient with Tuberculous Meningitis
pmc-12731431.creator: Sekai Tsujimoto, Koji Hayashi, Mamiko Sato, Yuka Nakaya, Toyoaki Miura, Yasutaka Kobayashi
pmc-12731431.description: A 30-year-old previously healthy man presented with fever and headache. HIV tests yielded negative results. Cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis revealed pleocytosis (619/µL), elevated protein (210.3 mg/dL) and adenosine deaminase levels, and decreased glucose levels. A positive CSF culture for tuberculosis confirmed the patient had tuberculous meningitis (TBM). He was treated with methylprednisolone, isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol (all highly sensitive).

pmc-12787016.description: The respiratory mucosal system plays a critical role in the pathogenesis of allergic asthma (AA). In this work, a plasmid encoding the Mycobacterium tuberculosis ESAT6-Fc fusion protein was successfully constructed, and high-purity ESAT6-Fc fusion protein was subsequently obtained.
